text:
alex: heads-up: after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak I see a 6-8% P50 regression on long-context workloads when using paged KV + bfloat16. appears only on A100 pools.

maya: ugh, can you paste the perf trace or a simple repro?

alex: repro is easy — checkout branch `opt/batch-merge`, run the 8k perf script against the paged-kv config. quick output: `p50 42.1ms -> 44.7ms` for batch=4 seq=8192. nvfuser kernels look identical, but attention selection flips to fused-flash-paged on hotpath.

lucas: sending nsys snippet, seems the issue is a memcpy spike inside `kv_page_load` when layout switches. flame shows extra strided loads and a bunch of `ld.global` stalls.

lucas: ```bash
# repro
GEMM_PRIORITY=1 KV_LAYOUT=paged KV_DTYPE=bfloat16 ./perf/run_inference.sh --model llama-13b --seq 8192 --batch 4
nsys profile -o tmp -t cuda,osrt,roctx -- ./perf/run_inference.sh ...
```

brian: interesting — our kernel selector picks fused-flash-paged based on avg_seq heuristic which assumed contiguous KV. if layout becomes interleaved inside the page (we changed page packing last week) the stride grows and fused kernel suffers from poor memory coalescing. :thinking:

alex: right. when I force `FORCE_KERNEL=flash-hybrid` we go back to baseline. so selector misclassifies.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: job/ci/perf/2026-03-16 detected +7% latency on model/llama-13b (A100). linked: https://ci.internal/reports/1950123

maya: can we have a quick mitigation: either prefer `flash-hybrid` for paged+bf16 when observed stride > 64 bytes, or add a cheap probe that samples page stride at runtime?

brian: probe sounds reasonable — add single-page sampling inside startup code: read first KV page pointer pattern and compute stride for r/o loads. if stride > threshold => prefer non-fused. low overhead.

lucas: also logging idea: emit `kv_stride_estimate` in the token latency events so we can correlate.

alex: logging + probe + hotfix for selector sounds good. I'll open a tiny PR with probe + default threshold 64. if someone can run a quick smoke on dev pool that would be great. :eyes:

maya: assigning to alex and brian. I'll run smoke on canary once PR is up.

brian: one more note: dtype affects memcpy size and alignment — bfloat16 halves element count but we still saw unaligned accesses due to page packing. our threshold might need to be dtype-aware.

alex: noted. PR will include dtype-aware stride calculation.

lucas: after hotfix let's run the full fused vs hybrid microbench on 1..8k sequences and post results. need curves not single points.

alex: thanks all — I'll ping when PR is ready.

perf-bot: triage: label=regression severity=medium owner=eng-runtime
